newsitem.title: FRANCE: HORSE RACING-AL CAPONE II ROMPS HOME IN GRAND STEEPLE-CHASE.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-AL CAPONE II ROMPS HOME IN GRAND STEEPLE-CHASE.

text.p: Al Capone II, France's record earning steeplechaser, finally won the Grand Steeple-Chase de Paris at Auteuil on Sunday after coming close twice in the past.
Previously placed twice in the race, the 2-1 ON shot was in devastating form as he crushed Cand d'Or by 10 lengths in the Gallic equivalent of the Cheltenham Gold Cup.
Al Capone II, ridden by Jean-Yves Beaurain, initially tracked his pace-setting arch-rival Chamberko, with the pair pulling some 15 lengths of the chasing pack.

But going into the final turn around three furlongs out, he took the lead and from then on ran his rivals ragged. Cand d'Or took second place, four lengths in front Gracky, who beat Chamberko into fourth.
Winning trainer Bernard Secly said: "Providing the owner consents and the horse is fine physically, it would be nice to keep him in training."
Earlier, the Queen Mother's novice chaser Fire Ball made it third time lucky in the Royal colours by landing an easy six-length success in the Prix Katko.
Fire Ball, ridden by Adam Kondrat and trained by Francois Doumen, had previously run fourth and third in the Royal colours.
